statements.text: What's clear is this: it's going to change the way we live. We have to determine how to make sure we end up on the right side of that change.
We can't afford for China to win the AI arms race; it has to be the United States.

Today, I’m excited to announce that I have introduced the K-12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026.

This bill updates our outdated education laws so schools can teach students the safe, responsible use of AI.  It also funds teacher training and professional development using existing federal dollars — zero new spending.

Let me be clear, we will not surrender our technological edge to China or anyone else. 

The future belongs to those who master AI, and today we’re ensuring America’s kids own it.

GREAT NEWS: My K-12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act passed out of the Education & Workforce Committee.

This bill builds strong foundational skills, empowers educators with real tools, promotes responsible AI use, and equips the next generation to dominate the global economy.

America’s best days are ahead, let’s get our kids ready to win.

I think it's largely an op by China. And let's explain why. So, I think the 21st century, who wins the 21st century, will largely be defined by who wins the war over AI. And that fight is on four levels.

But the fourth front in that fight is what they call compute: data centers. If you want to use Grok, if you want to use ChatGPT, if you want to use Claude and you type that stuff in, something needs to be doing the thinking. It's not happening on your phone. It's happening at a data center. And China has realized that if they can get America to not put data centers in, well then those data centers have to go in China, and China wins on that front of the war.

Does that mean you should be able to put a data center in a neighborhood? No, it doesn't. But does that mean the data centers are a critical part of re-industrializing the United States to make sure we win the war over AI? It absolutely is.

I introduced the K-12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act because federal funds still can’t be spent on AI education.

The law hasn’t been updated since before AI existed.

We need to set our kids up to get ahead with AI, not fall behind — and my bill does exactly that. https://t.co/8Q7cKildIX
